title: Expecting a monster to move like nothing else
target: How movement works in R.E.P.O. — the body every monster shares, the ones that tumble, and the three kinds of jump — so a monster's approach can be read rather than only survived.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A monster that is not walking

steps.do: Do not think of a monster as walking; think of its body following a target.
steps.because: a shared physical body follows a target rather than each monster owning its movement (EnemyRigidbody, enemy, followTarget)

steps.do: Expect some of them to fall differently.
steps.because: the body can use gravity or a gravity value of its own (gravity, customGravity)

steps.do: Notice that idling and chasing move differently, not only faster or slower.
steps.because: idle and chasing each have their own position and rotation speeds with their own smoothing, plus rotation damping (positionSpeedIdle, positionSpeedLerpIdle, positionSpeedChase, positionSpeedLerpChase, rotationSpeedIdle, rotationSpeedChase, rotationSpeedDamping)

steps.do: Give a monster room to warp, and watch for the distance at which it stops moving.
steps.because: there are separate warp distances for idle and for chasing, and a distance below which the body counts as not moving (distanceWarpIdle, distanceWarpChase, notMovingDistance)

steps.do: Expect at least one monster to come at you by tumbling rather than walking.
steps.because: a monster moves by tumbling rather than walking, with a tumble loop kept locally and across the level (EnemyTumbler, EnemyTumblerAnim, enemyTumbler, sfxTumbleLoopLocal, sfxTumbleLoopGlobal)

steps.do: Treat a jump as a behaviour with a surface, not as part of walking.
steps.because: jumping is its own behaviour with handling for the surface it lands on, an upward and a sideways force and a delay before and after (EnemyJump, EnemyJumpSurface, surfaceJumpForceUp, surfaceJumpForceSide, surfaceJumpDelay, surfaceLandDelay)

steps.do: Know that a monster stuck in one place behaves differently from one that is merely jumping.
steps.because: a stuck jump is limited by a count and has its own forces and delays (stuckJump, stuckJumpCount, stuckJumpForceUp, stuckJumpForceSide)

steps.do: Know that a gap is its own case as well.
steps.because: a gap jump has an upward and a forward force with its own delays, and landing can put the navigation agent back onto the surface (gapJump, gapJumpForceUp, gapJumpForceForward, warpAgentOnLand)

commonMistakes: Timing a swing as if every monster walked at the same pace.
Standing where a tumbling monster is about to roll.
Assuming a monster that jumped is committed to the spot it left.
Reading a stuck jump as the monster giving up.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
